newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Costello sees solid exports boost to Australia GDP.
newsitem.headline: Costello sees solid exports boost to Australia GDP.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Friday that March quarter GDP growth had gained a solid contribution from export data.

"Net export volumes rose from a A$244 million surplus to a A$864 million surplus with the result that net exports are estimated to contribute a solid 0.6 percent (points) to growth in expenditure-based GDP in the March quarter," Costello said in a statement.

Australia's current account deficit on the balance of payments was A$4.587 billion in the March quarter, down from A$5.262 billion in the December quarter, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said earlier.

The trade component of the balance of payments has implications for the expenditure-based GDP estimate, GDP-E. Since the balance of exports and imports (net exports) was stronger in the quarter, it implies more production in the economy.
The improvement was equivalent to 0.6 percent of GDP.
The bureau will publish its March quarter GDP estimates, averaging GDP-E with two other measures, on Wednesday.
